text:
opsbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: chi1 region - control-plane health degraded. API error rate 92% over 2m, kube node status churn, multiple pods evicted. Metrics: api_5xx=92%, node_not_ready=18. See dashboard: https://mon.redwood.example/chi1/controlplane

marco: Ack. Who's oncall for infra? @sre-rotation? Can we confirm external LB health and provider status?

jessica: I'm on it. Quick checks: control-plane API returning 502/503 from all AZs. kubectl to kube-system shows most api-server pods CrashLoopBackOff or NotReady. Sample: ```
$ kubectl get pods -n kube-system
kube-apiserver-az1   CrashLoopBackOff
kube-apiserver-az2   Running (unhealthy)
kube-controller-0    Evicted
kube-scheduler-1     NotReady
```

ravindra: autoscaler logs show repeated registration failures: TLS handshake timeouts + CNI errors. Provider network API reporting route withdraws for chi1. I'm opening provider ticket now.

marco: Marking incident Sev2 and starting regional failover runbook. Primary goal: restore API for customer traffic by shifting inference routing and control-plane proxies out of chi1.

jessica: Proposed actions (initial):
- Lock control-plane config (no rollouts).
- Pause any autoscaler/descheduler jobs.
- Shift model-serving traffic off chi1 immediately (failover to sfo1).
- Start reserved capacity spin-up in sfo1 for critical tenants.

marco: Execute traffic shift. Use traffic-manager: ```
traffic-manager promote-region --from chi1 --to sfo1 --mode immediate --route-type inference --dry-run=false
traffic-manager set-weight --region sfo1 --weight 100 --routes inference-*,chat-*
```

opsbot: Note: sfo1 current committed reserved pool at 62% used. Burstpool available: 200 gpus (reserved-dedicated). Approvals required from infra leads for burst.

ravindra: I'm provisioning burst capacity in sfo1 now. Cloud-provider ticket opened: CSP-CH-48291. Provider message: "We are seeing fabric instability and route flaps in chi1, escalated to network team." ETA unknown.

jessica: Rolling restart of control-plane pods could help only after provider stabilizes network. For now avoid full restarts to prevent split-brain. Focus on routing and capacity.

marco: Noted. I'll ping sales & support to throttle new signups and mark chi1 degraded on status.redwood.com. Also opening internal customer banner.

sre-rotation: Paging network oncall and cloud account manager. @cloud-support-bot please surface CSP escalation contact and open a high-severity bridge.

cloud-support-bot: CSP contact: network-escalations@cloud.example (bridge ID: br-98123). Provider assigned engineer: Anika Rao. Bridge scheduled now.

jessica: Started runbook step: failover control-plane proxies (edge) by updating proxy pool to remove chi1. Command: ```
proxyctl remove-region chi1 --services control-proxy --force
proxyctl add-region sfo1 --services control-proxy --weight 100
```

ravindra: Spawning reserved instances in sfo1: `provisioner create --region sfo1 --gpu-type a100 --count 120 --label reserved-failover` logs show nodes coming up, kubelet joining. Approx 6m until pods scheduled.

marco: Good. Customer-facing fallback: route inference traffic to sfo1+nyc1 with sticky session disabled to avoid cache warmup. Notify caching team to rehydrate critical prefixes.

opsbot: Alert: cost impact estimate for immediate failover + burst capacity ~ $32k/day if sustained. Flagging finance for potential spike.

jessica: Ticket update: provider bridge confirms fabric flaps causing control-plane pod network partitions. They recommend waiting for fiber failover and have no ETA beyond "under investigation".

marco: Action items assigned:
- ravindra: continue provisioning and verify node health (in progress).
- jessica: run proxy failover and coordinate cache rehydration (in progress).
- sre-rotation: keep bridge and escalate with provider (in progress).
- opsbot: update status page and throttle signups (in progress).

sre-rotation: Declaring incident, Sev2 -> Incident channel created, paging execs. Next update in 5 minutes unless status changes.

marco: Thanks team. If provider gives ETA, we'll assess whether to bring a subset of services back to chi1 or keep running on fallback. Avoid schema migrations or control-plane writes until fully stable.

opsbot: Acknowledged. Recording incident start=1815001234. Will post next automated summary at 1815001534.
